title: Capituli Graeci De decem Dei nominibus. Aliud et melius exemplar
author: Incertus

passages.original: Nomen περασμ'ω;, quod, in fine, interpretatus sum, quia πέρας finis ac terminus dicitur, οίπεπε- pζεμένος apud Aristotelem finitus vel terminatus intelligitur, quomodo scriptum reperi in codice Colbertino, sic illud edidi quasi esset adverbium. Sumpto autem adverbialiter nomine περασμίω,*, necesario subintelligendum existimavi nomen γλώτταν, ut phrasis Graeca seusus complemento gau- deret.
passages.english: The word *perasmiōs*, which I have translated "in the end" (because *peras* means "end" and "limit", and *peperasmenos* in Aristotle is understood as "finite" or "limited"), I have printed as I found it written in the Colbertine codex, as though it were an adverb. Taking the word *perasmiōs* adverbially, however, I judged that the word *glōttan* ["tongue"] must necessarily be understood, so that the Greek phrase might have the completion of its sense.
passages.notes: The Greek is badly garbled by the scan: "περασμ'ω;" and "περασμίω,*" are taken as περασμίως (the form named in the context after); "οίπεπε- pζεμένος" is read as πεπερασμένος (Aristotle's term for "finite"). Other scanning errors corrected: "seusus" as sensus, "gau- deret" as gauderet, "necesario" as necessario. The phrase "sensus complemento gauderet" is literally "might enjoy the completion of its sense".
